raw_response:
I’m farming only 2 mu, and at my age I’m not going to gamble too much. Chili can make money if the stand is good and disease stays under control, but it also eats labor and input money. My family has only 2 people and some work off-farm, so I need a plan I can manage without spending too much cash at once. I’ll keep the full 2 mu in chili, use a variety I know people around here plant, put enough base fertilizer so the seedlings start strong, then topdress in a few rounds depending on how the plants look. Since I have a well, I’m not as worried about dry spells, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate blindly. If rain is decent, I save one watering. Pesticide I won’t spray on a calendar like big farms do; I’ll watch for aphids, thrips, and disease, then use medicine when I really see pressure. For me the main thing is steady production and not getting caught short on cash.
